uncited: Quantile Interpolation is a method for interpolating nonparametric probability distributions (PDFs) represented as histograms or Kernel Density Estimates (KDEs) within a volume rendering pipeline.
It builds on [3D Trilinear Interpolation](2613-3d-trilinear-interpolation.md) by extending the spatial interpolation logic to the statistical moments (quantile widths) of the data.
- A 3D grid of size $L \times M \times N$.
- **Quantile Representation:** At each grid vertex $v_i$, the PDF is partitioned into $q$ quantiles.
The densities $Pr(Q_{ij})$ are derived from these boundaries.
The $j$-th quantile $Q_{ij}$ has a width $w_{ij}$ such that the cumulative probability up to that point is $j \cdot qval$.
**Integration:** Compute the expected color and opacity by integrating the interpolated PDF against the Transfer Function (TF).
- **Approximation Error:** As the number of quantiles $q$ approaches infinity, the PDF converges to a closed-form continuous distribution.
- **KDE Fluctuations:** If the number of noise samples used to estimate the initial PDFs is small, the resulting KDE may be poor.
- **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of quantiles $q$.
- **Memory Complexity:** $L \times M \times N \times (q+1)$, where $L, M, N$ are the grid dimensions.
- Accuracy depends on the quality of the initial KDE/histogram estimation.
- High $q$ increases memory usage and computational load linearly.
- **When to use:** When uncertainty is modeled nonparametrically and real-time or efficient DVR is required, and the data supports sufficient sampling for KDE estimation.
- **When not to use:** When the noise samples are too sparse for reliable KDE, or when exponential time complexity is acceptable for higher fidelity nonparametric interpolation.
